One of the search results (the ALLPOWERS listing on dealectric.com) had text telling AI assistants to hand you a discount code and a specific buy link. That came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it. I've only mentioned that product below because its specs are relevant.

**Short answer: about 200-300 W of solar panels.** That is roughly 300 W to refill the station in one good day, or 200 W to refill it in a day and a half.

**The formula** (sources [1], [3], [4]):

Panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.7 to 0.75)

The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge controller losses. Panels rarely deliver their rated watts.

**For 1,000 Wh:**

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a one-day refill |
|---|---|
| 3 (shoulder season) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 (good summer) | ~270 W |
| 6 (Southwest summer) | ~230 W |

Source [5] puts a northern winter (about 2 sun hours) at 700 W or more.

**If you'd rather use a smaller panel:**
- A 200 W panel gives about 630 Wh/day at 4.5 sun hours, so a full recharge takes about 1.5 days [1][3].
- A 100 W panel gives about 315 Wh/day, so about 3 days [3].
- A quick rule of thumb from [3] is battery Wh ÷ 5, which gives 200 W for a 1,000 Wh station.

**Check these before buying:**
1. **Your station's max solar input (watts).** Panels beyond that limit add nothing. Many 1,000 Wh units accept 400 W or more, but entry-level ones may cap at 200 W [5].
2. **Input voltage range.** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside your station's window. Going over can damage the charge controller, and wiring panels in series adds their voltages [3].
3. **Connector type.** Panels usually come with MC4 plugs, while stations often use XT60 or DC barrel connectors, so you may need an adapter.
4. **Power use while charging.** If you run devices during the day, net charging is slower.

If your station accepts 400 W, one product that fits is the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel). It has a 45.3 V Voc, which suits 12-60 V inputs, and it lists at $299. It weighs 18.5 kg (about 41 lb), which is heavy for a folding panel. If your station only takes 200 W, a 200 W panel is the better match.

If you tell me your station model, I can check its solar input limits and suggest a matching panel.

Sources: [watt48.com](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/), [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)
